newsitem.title: FRANCE: Alcatel wins $135 mln Russian deal.
newsitem.headline: Alcatel wins $135 mln Russian deal.

text.p: French company Alcatel Telecom, a unit of Alcatel Alsthom, said on Wednesday it had won a contract valued at $135 million that was the largest ever order for a digital cellular system in Russia.

"This contract is a new milestone in the development of mobile communications in Russia as it is by far the largest contract ever signed in Russia in terms of size and investment," Alcatel said in a statement.

The DCS 1800 contract was awarded by KB Impuls, a unit of VimpelCom,the largest cellular operator in Russia and CIS which groups all the former Soviet Republics. Last month, VimpelCom became the first Russian company to be listed on the New York Stock Exchange.
It is Russia's first DCS 1800 mobile communications network for which KB Impuls obtained a 10-year licence in May 1996.
"This is a very important deal for Alcatel in Russia and the contract belongs 100 percent to Alcatel," a spokeswoman for Alcatel Telecom said.
Under the contract, Alcatel will supply on a full turnkey basis a DCS 1800 mobile communications network in the greater Moscow area which covers a population of 18 million.
The planned capacity of the network is 380,000 subscribers.
The first phase of the network has been built over the last six months and is currently being tested while commerical operation is scheduled to begin in March 1997.

Russia is a strategic market for Alcatel and "with this new contract, Alcatel is now the number one GSM/DCS cellular supplier in the country with three other GSM networks already operational," the company said.
